newsitem.title: UK: Mexico PRI stalwart seen new ambassador to London.
newsitem.headline: Mexico PRI stalwart seen new ambassador to London.

text.p: Britain said on Wednesday it has given its approval for former Mexican ruling party president Santiago Onate to become ambassador to London, pending confirmation by the Mexican senate.
"The queen has given agrement," a foreign office official told Reuters. Britain's Queen Elizabeth has to approve the appointment of foreign ambassadors on the recommendation of her foreign minister.
Mexico's senate has yet to give its approval, but government sources say this is expected to take place on April 3, allowing Onate to take up the post in May.

Onate, 47, was the president of Mexico's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) from August 1995 until December last year. Before that he was President Ernesto Zedillo's first labour minister, between December 1994 and August 1995, and was Mexico's representative to the Organsiation of American States from 1991 to 1992.
Onate replaces career diplomat Andres Rozental, who is returning to Mexico in May. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
